subject: Model Selection Order and Reporting Covariate Estimates

messages.author: 5808bc1ac10b9387
messages.subject: Model Selection Order and Reporting Covariate Estimates
parts:
Hi Jeff,

I am in the process of conducting a stPGOcc() and have a question about the order in which I should be conducting the two sub-models. I have found only a handful of papers that actually explain the order in which they find the top models for their detection and occupancy sub-models. In these examples, they hold a global occupancy model constant to first find the top performing detection model, then hold said detection model constant to find the top performing occupancy sub-model. So the step-wise process would be 1) run all combination detection probability models with global occ model, 2) run all combination occupancy models with top performing detection model from step 1. That makes sense to me, but then in which model do you report your det probability covariate estimates? 

For example, if I am looking at the effects of PM2.5 concentration on black bear detection probability, would I report the estimate from the top performing detection sub-model (assuming PM2.5 is in that model) that has the global occ model, or should I instead report estimates from the top performing occupancy sub-model in step 2? I guess my main question is whether the "complete" occupancy model is considered the top model from "step 2." Let me know if I need to clarify anything and thank you for your time!

Best,
Clayton

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: Model Selection Order and Reporting Covariate Estimates
parts:
Hi Clayton, 

Thanks for the message. In such a situation, you would want to report estimates from the top-performing model in step 2. More generally, note that stepwise selection has a fair number of problems so if you haven't already I'd encourage you to read some resources on those limitations prior to interpreting results from the analysis (like this paper). 

Kind regards,

Jeff
